ev.q: Analysis of CDC-funded program data submitted by 61 health departments in 2015
Among the 1,798 women with newly diagnosed HIV infection, 1,104 (61%) were linked to HIV medical care within 90 days
Rates for linkage to medical care within 90 days of the current test date were 61% and 58%
Compared with women aged 20–29 years, those aged 13–19 years were less likely to receive a new diagnosis
A high percentage of women tested had already received an HIV diagnosis (62%)
was lower for black women (57%) than for white women (65%; aPR = 0.91)
Multivariate robust Poisson regression ( 4 ) was used to assess the association between demographic characteristics and newly diagnosed HIV infections
Data were stratified by the following demographic characteristics: age group, race/ethnicity, census region
Analysis of CDC-funded program data submitted by 61 health departments in 2015
Health departments submitted deidentified program data about services provided by both health departments and CBOs

methods_quotes.q: Multivariate robust Poisson regression ( 4 ) was used to assess the association between demographic characteristics and newly diagnosed HIV infections
Data were stratified by the following demographic characteristics: age group, race/ethnicity, census region, health department jurisdiction’s prevalence of HIV infection, and test setting.
Analyses excluded discordant and indeterminate results.
